messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing a lot of support asks about confusing cost/latency badges when folks open per-route saved views. Proposing a single 'capacity hint' line that explains: expected token burn, likely latency tier, and whether the route is eligible for Dedicated fallback. Short and actionable.

Priya: +1 to a single line. Current badges are too noisy. Can we make it driven by server telemetry so it updates with real usage? :thinking:

Marco: Driven server-side sounds right. But we need to decide if the saved-query payload should capture the hint snapshot or always compute on load. If snapshot, product folks can pin the hint for audits. If compute-on-load, it's fresher but can mislead during rollouts.

Jules: Leaning compute-on-load with an optional "snapshot_hint" field in the saved-query model. That gives both behaviors. UX: show a small "snapshotted at T" tooltip when snapshot used.

Sam: Implementation note: telemetry sampling means we might not have immediate accurate percentiles for rare routes. We should include a confidence score (low/med/high) next to latency.

Priya: Good call. Confidence would help. Also add a simple heuristic: if recent sample size < 50, show "low confidence" and include a link to run an immediate sample.

Marco: About API shape — draft payload I sketched:

```
{
  "query_id": "q_123",
  "filters": { "route": "invoices/*", "model": "redwood-v2-opt" },
  "hint": {
    "mode": "computed", // or "snapshotted"
    "latency_p50_ms": 120,
    "latency_p95_ms": 420,
    "expected_tokens_per_call": 340,
    "confidence": "low"
  }
}
```

If we include this, console can render without an extra call. But storage size per-saved-query bumps.

Lina: Storage isn't huge concern but we need to hash which model variant the hint refers to. Otherwise the hint becomes stale when model pinned/unpinned. Maybe add "model_variant_id" and rollout tag.

Alex: Good catch. Also need to handle routing policy fallbacks: hint should say if route will fall back to cheaper model under high load. That affects dev expectations.

Jules: UX idea: tiny pill that reads "Fallback: yes (to redwood-lite)" with an expand for explanation. Default collapsed.

Sam: On quota and Dedicated eligibility — should hint say "Quota risk: high" if usage rate close to bucket? We can compute burn = token_rate * qps. If burn > 80% of quota, mark high. But teams may find it scary. Suggest soft language: "quota pressure: moderate" and link to mitigation docs.

Priya: Also call out when a route's autoscale policy will prevent spikes (i.e., Dedicated + burst). So show "Autoscale: enabled (burst ok)" vs "Strict quota: true".

Marco: Rollout plan: feature flag on server to compute hint and store snapshot when saving. Console reads either snapshot or computes on render based on a query param. Start with internal-only rollout then 10% production.

Alex: For telemetry, let's avoid new heavy sampling. Use existing route metrics + a quick-on-demand sample endpoint if team clicks "refresh hint". That keeps costs down.

Lina: Edge-case: offline/private deployments (Private) won't have access to global telemetry. We should fall back to local agent heuristics and indicate scope in hint: "data_source: private-agent".

Jules: Accessibility note: avoid relying only on color-coded badges. Add text and aria-labels.

Sam: One quick API debate: should the console request include the full saved-query filters or a saved-query id? If id, server can fill latest filters+model mapping. If full filters, console gets deterministic response but more payload. I'm for id-only to centralize logic.

Priya: I vote id-only with an optional "force_refresh": true param to run an immediate sampling job.

Marco: Canary plan: rollout-bot, can we gate this behind a rollout that checks route traffic classes? We should avoid showing computed hints for extremely low-traffic routes by default.

rollout-bot: Canary rollout started for feature "console_capacity_hint" — 10% of orgs, exclude low-traffic routes. (deployment id: r-202) :rocket:

Alex: Nice. For saved-query schema migration we'll add new columns: hint_mode, hint_blob, hint_generated_at, hint_source. Migration script should be small.

Lina: Can we also add telemetry tags so we can later query how often hints were stale vs helpful? Event: hint_refreshed, hint_used_in_decision.

Jules: UX microcopy workshop: needs to be careful about telling customers they're over quota. Avoid alarmist text. Put mitigation steps in-place. I'll draft copy.

Priya: Action items: 1) Marco and Sam to spec server API and migration. 2) Jules + Alex to prototype UI pill and microcopy. 3) Lina to define telemetry events. 4) I'll create the feature flag and rollout plan.

Alex: Thanks — will follow up with a quick Figma and a short RFC. :thumbsup:

Lina: Also tagging @eng-sre to keep them in loop for quota calculation sanity checks.

Sam: Quick note: add unit tests around fallback detection logic — caught a live bug last week.

Marco: I'll drop a working API swagger by EOD.

Jules: Mini-UX check: show examples for "low confidence" vs "high confidence" states in the prototype.

Alex: End of thread — thanks all.
